newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Autoways says in Indian power project.
newsitem.headline: Autoways says in Indian power project.

text.p: Malaysia's Autoways Holdings Bhd said on Monday its wholly-owned unit has entered into an agreement to subscribe for 70 percent equity in an Indian company which is building a power generating plant.

Autoways Construction Sdn Bhd plans to subscribe for shares in Tanir Bavi Power Company which has the rights to build a 163 megawatt barge-mounted plant in Mangalore, in Karnataka state, Autoways said in a statement.
Other shareholders with 10 percent equity each are Sea Corp, Chicago Power Inc and Kontek Abadi Sdn Bhd. The statement did not mention the nationalities of the other companies.
Under a separate agreement to be signed, the Karnataka Electricity Board will buy from Tanir Bavi at least 85 percent of electricity generated from the project for seven years.
Tanir Bavi will also be granted a tax holiday of five years, Autoways said.
The total cost of the project is estimated at $160 million. Autoways said based on a preliminary study, the project is expected to generate after-tax profit of $12 million annually.
Commercial operations is expected to start 12 months after the signing of the agreement with the electricity board.
Tanir Bavi has authorised capital of 10 million rupees.
Autoways, involved in trading of rubber based products and machinery and construction, requested for immediate lifting of trading suspension of its stock from the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange.
The stock was suspended from December 24, being last traded at 22.00 ringgit.
